content: We have carbon NMR data: chemical shifts list. Need number of CH3 groups in the molecule. From carbon NMR, methyl carbons appear around 10-30 ppm (aliphatic). In list we have 19.23 ppm likely a methyl. Also maybe 43.55, 49.55, 52.24 are methylene or quaternary? Those are higher. So only one methyl? But need to be sure. Could also be 52.24 maybe O-CH3 (methoxy) also methyl. O-methyl appears ~55 ppm. So 52.24 could be a methoxy methyl. That would be a CH3 attached to O. So there could be two methyls: one at 19.23 (alkyl) and one at 52.24 (O-CH3). Also 43.55 maybe a carbon attached to heteroatom (like N-CH3) appears ~40 ppm. Could be N-methyl. So there could be three methyls. Need to infer structure? Let's retrieve carbon shift ranges for functional groups.
